portInfo.description: La Romana’s cruise facility is a privately operated river-mouth terminal run by Central Romana Corporation, which also owns the historic sugar industrial complex. The operator’s technical sheet distinguishes a West Berth (sugar/molasses) from an East Berth used exclusively for cruise ships, with published pier length 256 m and maximum ship dimensions 360 × 61 m and 226,000 GT, channel entrance 11.5 m and maximum draft 10.5 m, 24/7 operations, and ISPS certification coded DOLRM / DOLRM-0001 (certificate dated 26 May 2006). Marketing pages position the port as both a port of call and a homeport with integrated transfers to La Romana International Airport (LRM), claiming ~45 minutes to Punta Cana and ~90 minutes to Santo Domingo. Cruise operations at Catalina Island (from 1992 with Costa) and the East Berth cruise pier (from 2002) are part of the same corporate story — for SeaDays mapping, keep la-romana-dominican-republic on the river terminal unless a separate Catalina slug is confirmed.
